title: RL retries only the targets 1 loop failed, each at 2, 4 or 8 loops chosen at random
description: Pretraining and the RL fine-tune are the incumbent's. Only where rl() spends its samples changes. Each round every target gets 8 attempts at 1 loop; the targets all 8 fail on are shuffled and dealt into three equal groups, which get 24 more attempts at 2, 4 and 8 loops respectively (32 attempts in all, as before). The incumbent gave every target 8 attempts at each of 1, 2, 4 and 8 loops, so after the first fine-tune most of its 2/4/8-loop samples went to targets that 1 loop had already solved in that round. Rounds get shorter as the failed set shrinks, so more of them fit in RL_SECS (the round rule is unchanged). rl() also returns, for each retry call, how many of its targets got a proof.
hypothesis: Two claims. (1) Allocation: deep samples are the expensive ones (an 8-loop sample costs about 2.5x a 2-loop one) and in 500 they bought little once the model was fine-tuned: in round 3 the 8-loop call added 12 newly solved targets for about 75 s. Spending 2/4/8-loop attempts only on targets that just resisted 1 loop keeps 32 attempts per resistant target while cutting a late round's sampling from about 183 s to about 70 s, so about 7 rounds fit where 5 did, and the spike's models kept gaining from extra rounds (657 to 700 at 8 loops between round 4 and round 12). More rounds over the same targets should solve more long RL targets and raise dev at 8 loops. (2) Measurement: the failed targets are assigned to 2, 4 or 8 loops at random with equal attempts, so a round's three retry calls are a controlled comparison of loop counts on targets the shallow pass could not solve, at every stage of RL. If depth does real work on hard problems, 8 loops should crack more of them than 2 loops in every round, not only before the first fine-tune.
expected_delta: metric at 8 loops +5 to +25 over 675 (3-seed mean about 680-700); 6 or 7 RL rounds per seed against 500's 5/5/4; cumulative RL targets solved 1180-1260 against 1149. Retry comparison: in round 1 (pretrained model) the 8-loop retry acceptance rate is at least 1.3x the 2-loop rate; from round 3 on the 8-loop and 2-loop retry rates are within 10% of each other, i.e. depth stops helping on resistant targets once the model is fine-tuned, as the spike saw on never-solved targets. metric minus metric_diag stays near 500's +18 (10 to 25): this change is about where RL samples go and is not expected to widen the 8-vs-2 gap at eval. Fewer samples go to easy targets, so fewer distinct proofs per easy target is the main risk. Discard if the 3-seed mean is not above 675.

arch.type: looped gpt: 1 entry + 2 shared core x n + 1 exit Peri-LN blocks, LayerNorm(state)+entry re-injection per loop

optimizer.name: muon (polar express) on block matrices and head + adamw on the rest

config.init: orthogonal on block matrices, fork default elsewhere

rl.samples_note: 8 at 1 loop for every target; 24 more at one of 2/4/8 loops only for targets whose 8 one-loop attempts all failed that round, so a target 1 loop solves gets 8
rl.retry_assignment: failed targets shuffled with the run's rng, dealt round-robin to 2, 4, 8
rl.rounds: until another round would not fit in RL_SECS (expected 6-7)
rl.ft_optimizer: adamw, warmup 50 then cosine to lr/10
rl.loss: next-token CE on the last loop's output

rl.oracle: Lean AND nd_verify accepted samples of the model's own attempts

eval.metric: dev-transfer theorems solved at L_true >= 7 with KNOB at EVAL_LEVEL
